C08-M04-L05-F1.title: Recursive resolution: where a query is logged and who receives it
C08-M04-L05-F1.caption: One DNS lookup relayed by the internal resolver to the zone's authoritative server, showing why the query name itself reaches whoever controls the zone.
C08-M04-L05-F1.alt: Sequence diagram with four lanes: Workstation WS-104 (stub resolver), Internal resolver (query log written here), Root / TLD servers (referrals only) and Authoritative for t.example (whoever controls the zone). The workstation sends 'Query: <label>.t.example TXT?' to the internal resolver. The resolver sends 'Same query (recursion)' to the root and TLD servers, which reply with a dashed 'Referral: ask ns1.t.example'. The resolver sends 'Query forwarded to ns1.t.example' to the authoritative server, which replies with a dashed 'Answer: TXT data / or NXDOMAIN'. The resolver returns a dashed 'Answer relayed (and cached for TTL)' to the workstation.
C08-M04-L05-F1.note: The full name, labels included, reaches the zone's owner without any direct connection from the workstation.

C08-M04-L05-F2.title: DNS anomaly patterns: evidence, innocent twins and next checks
C08-M04-L05-F2.caption: A triage reference for the six DNS patterns in this lesson, pairing each with its common benign look-alike and the check that decides.
C08-M04-L05-F2.alt: Table with columns Pattern, In the log, Benign look-alike and Next check. Row 1 (red): NXDOMAIN burst; many random names fail from one client; typos, browser start-up probes; find the NOERROR success and its answer. Row 2 (red): Long high-entropy labels; labels near 63 characters, hex or Base32; CDN and security-product lookups; parent zone age and rarity. Row 3 (red): Many subdomains, one parent; hundreds of unique names under one zone; CDN parent zones across many hosts; how many clients ask, total name bytes. Row 4 (orange): High TXT share; steady TXT or NULL queries from a workstation; mail servers, SPF/DMARC checks; client role and asking process. Row 5 (orange): Direct or encrypted DNS; port 53 or 853 to outside, DoH to a provider; unmanaged or misconfigured device; asset inventory and egress policy. Row 6 (violet): Newly seen domain; first query for the name in the estate; new SaaS service adopted; registration age, who else asked, what followed.
